clue.text: Girl's witty outburst

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, with the 's standing for 'is' to join the two senses
a quip or sudden flash of wit

explanation.surface: Someone's daughter comes out with a clever remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sally is a common female name, and a sally is also a quick retort or burst of repartee.

clue.text: Surprising, putting acid in drink

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a sling is a sweetened spirit drink, as in the Singapore sling
tart means sharp or acid in taste

explanation.surface: Someone shockingly laces a cocktail with acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling things astonish or alarm.

clue.text: Slip in ballet — no end of confusion

indicators.note: confusion jumbles the remaining letters
the dance's name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A dancer trips mid-performance, causing endless chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' drops T from BALLET, leaving BALLE, and 'confusion' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of paper attached to a parcel carries a label, a tag or ticket.

clue.text: Light goes up on: opening this resort

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
a mouth is an opening, as of a river

explanation.surface: Lights come on at the start of the season in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns RAY into YAR. Great Yarmouth is a seaside resort in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Yarmouth is an English seaside holiday town on the Norfolk coast.

clue.text: Craft intended for a sailor

parts.note: a craft is a boat
one's intended is a sweetheart or suitor, an old word for which is swain

explanation.surface: A vessel was built specially for a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' looks like a verb meaning designed, but it is the noun: a fiancé or suitor, which old poetry calls a SWAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain (bosun) is the ship's officer in charge of rigging and deck crew, so a kind of seaman.

clue.text: Vessel from the Isle of Dogs?

definitions.meaning: a sailing ship, also spelt barque
what comes from dogs is their cry

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district of London's docklands, so a ship from there fits the surface, but the second sense is simply the noise dogs make.
explanation.definitionFit: A bark is a three-masted ship, and the sound a dog makes is also a bark.

clue.text: Refraining from sin can't be bad, East concludes

indicators.note: East comes at the conclusion of the answer
bad as in poorly made, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A preacher in the East argues that holding back from wrongdoing is no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges SINCANTBE and 'concludes' puts E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is holding back from indulgence, especially drink.

clue.text: Ape-like object is, coming up North:

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an object or purpose

explanation.surface: A thing is being hauled up from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns AIMIS into SIMIA, and N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Simian describes monkeys and apes or their features.

clue.text: Victim of the first joker

parts.note: the first is not the original prankster but the first day of the fourth month, when tricks are played

explanation.definitionFit: Someone fooled by a prank on the first of April.

clue.text: Celebrated as certain bars. would be.?

definitions.meaning: bars of music are written with notes on them

explanation.definitionFit: A famous person is noted, and a musical bar is literally filled with written notes.

clue.text: Garb miser mended in part of Moby Dick

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are repaired into a new order

explanation.surface: A stingy man's clothes are patched while he reads Melville's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance formed in the gut of the sperm whale, the species of Melville's white whale.

clue.text: Learned deserter was a revolutionary

parts.note: a learned person may hold an MA, a Master of Arts degree
a rat is one who deserts a cause, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A scholar who turned traitor had once been a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution, stabbed in his bath in 1793.

clue.text: Add about a pound from this Great War house

indicators.note: the word for add is placed around the other pieces, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: to tot up is to add
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Sum up the cost of a wartime building, with a pound or so knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: Talbot House, at Poperinge in Belgium, was a soldiers' rest club in the First World War, the origin of the Toc H movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Talbot House was the famous First World War soldiers' club in Flanders, known by its signallers' name Toc H.

clue.text: B, a seaman who's incapacitated ?

parts.note: an able seaman is written AB; take away the A for 'able' and only B is left, a sailor who has lost his ability

explanation.walkthrough: AB stands for able seaman. With the A (able) gone, B is a seaman who has been 'dis-abled', which is the answer read in two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the use of a limb or faculty means unable, hence incapacitated.

clue.text: :Weapon widely used ?

parts.note: a blade with a wide edge, read too as a term in broad use

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'widely used' describes a word in broad use as well as a sword wielded with a wide blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-bladed cutting sword.

clue.text: It's all right maybe getting a danger signal, but unlucky

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of these words could be arranged some other way

parts.note: a red light or flag signals danger

explanation.surface: Someone told everything is fine sees a warning light, and is out of luck after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns ITSALL into ILLSTA; then R and RED follow. 'It's all right' wants to be one phrase, but its last word is split off as R.
explanation.definitionFit: To be born under an evil star is to be doomed to misfortune, so ill-fated.

clue.text: Dull and unsettled on rising in Welsh resort

indicators.note: the letters of these words are disturbed into a new arrangement
in a down clue rising means reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A dreary Welsh seaside town grows restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges DULLAND and 'rising' turns ON into NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a seaside town on the north coast of Wales.

clue.text: The band for a bowler ?

parts.note: a bowler sounds like a cricketer or a hat with a hatband, but here it is a child bowling a ring along with a stick

explanation.walkthrough: Children once bowled a large wooden or metal ring along the street with a stick; the ring is a band in the sense of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's ring for bowling along the ground, also a circular band round a barrel.

clue.text: Offered as arms might be?

definitions.meaning: soldiers hold rifles upright before them in salute on the order to present arms

explanation.definitionFit: Something presented is offered or given, and rifles held up in salute have been presented on parade.

clue.text: Before ten, going to' church — that's the claim.

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone says they will be at church before ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a false profession or claim to something.

clue.text: Poet in the shade

definitions.meaning: Thomas ... wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
a colour between black and white, spelt with an A in American usage

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray is the eighteenth-century English elegist, and gray is a neutral colour midway between black and white.

clue.text: Song is another included by abler composers

indicators.note: the second piece is placed inside the first
composers are people who put things together, so the letters of abler are composed afresh

parts.note: the clue's song is followed by another song, a carol

explanation.surface: A tune is taken up by more skilful writers of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composers' looks like the musicians; it makes BARLE from ABLER, and 'included by' puts CAROL inside after BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarolle is a Venetian gondolier's boating song or a piece in that rocking style.

clue.text: Native 'conference of first class standing includes band members

annotationWithheld.why: Native 'conference of first class standing includes band members (6), INDABA: first-class A1 reversed (IA) round NDAB, but no reading of 'band members' gives NDAB and no source gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Native 'conference of first class standing includes band members

clue.text: It's Enid's change of order

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made to change places

explanation.surface: A girl named Enid gets a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness and good arrangement are what tidiness means, as in keeping a room in order.

clue.text: Object of play, for Hamlet

definitions.meaning: Hamlet says the play's the ... to catch the conscience of the king

explanation.definitionFit: Thing means an object, and Hamlet's line 'The play's the thing' equates the play with it.

clue.text: Firm: supplying horses ?

definitions.meaning: a riding or racing establishment that keeps and provides horses

explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and secure, and a stable is the building or yard where horses are kept and hired out.

clue.text: An assassin, in general

definitions.meaning: William ... founded the Salvation Army and was its first General

explanation.definitionFit: John Wilkes Booth killed President Lincoln, and General William Booth led the Salvation Army.

clue.text: Actor turns up in foyer at seven:

indicators.note: turns up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer appears in the theatre lobby at seven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run RATS inside 'foyer at seven', and 'turns up', read upwards in a down clue, reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading performer is called a star.

clue.text: At home day for. Spaniard in: country

parts.note: to be at home is to be in
dia is the Spanish word for day

explanation.surface: A Spanish visitor takes a day at home in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation of South Asia.

clue.text: Striking duet, : definitely

definitions.meaning: two workers on strike are each out, a pair of outs joined

explanation.walkthrough: A worker on strike is 'out'; a duet of strikers is one out and another out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means complete or absolute, as in an out-and-out villain.

clue.text: Bird is a male one includes duck, very 'big'

indicators.note: the male bird's name holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a gander is a male goose, the bird being the 'one'
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: This large bird is a drake that has a duck in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a nil score in cricket, hence O, and OS is the clothing label for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a large fish-eating sawbill duck of northern waters.

clue.text: Hoped to'repair: vestment

indicators.note: to repair is to put right, so these letters are put in their right order

explanation.surface: A priest had hopes of mending a robe.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephod is a sleeveless garment worn by the ancient Jewish high priest.
